articles.title: Festival Transformar em Santos: Programação gratuita até domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: A programação reúne oficinas de fotografia, teatro, gastronomia e sustentabilidade, além de exposições, apresentações culturais e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas. As atividades são gratuitas e acontecem no Sesc Santos e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, até domingo (15).
articles.summary: O Festival Transformar Santos oferece oficinas de fotografia, gastronomia e feira criativa com 60 marcas na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro e no Sesc até este domingo.
articles.body:
Também será possível participar de uma oficina que acompanhará os bastidores do 'Documentário Transformar' — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

A cidade de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, recebe até domingo (15) a terceira edição do Festival Transformar, com programação gratuita voltada à cultura, educação, sustentabilidade e economia criativa. Entre as atrações, há oficinas, apresentações culturais, exposições e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas.

Idealizado por Gabriel Del Corso e realizado pela Re-Set.br, o festival tem o apoio do Senac Santos e do Sesc Santos. O Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa da Natureza (IBDN) é parceiro nas ações de neutralização de carbono.

A programação começou na quarta-feira (11), com atividades no Sesc Santos, no bairro Aparecida, e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva. Entre os destaques, estão oficinas de fotografia, teatro, customização de roupas, gastronomia e alimentação saudável.

As atividades são gratuitas e têm vagas limitadas. A programação é dividida entre o Sesc Santos, na Rua Conselheiro Ribas, nº 136, e a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, ambos no bairro Aparecida.

As inscrições para as oficinas do Senac estão disponíveis no site da instituição. As demais atividades têm inscrições e condições específicas de participação.

O núcleo Mar Aberto — Futuros em Circulação oferece atividades em diferentes áreas. Confira alguns dos temas:

Customização de roupas e reaproveitamento de tecidos;

Culinária caiçara e alimentação saudável;

Laboratório audiovisual para produção de minidocumentários;

Painel sobre desenvolvimento sustentável e governança colaborativa.

Até sábado (14), das 11h às 21h, a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva recebe o núcleo Viva Circular, com mais de 60 marcas de gastronomia, arte, moda, design e outros segmentos.

O espaço também terá exposições, música, atividades culturais gratuitas e iniciativas de afroempreendedorismo do Coletivo AfroTu.

Unidade Sesc Santos. — Foto: Divulgação/Sesc

articles.title: Kathy Ireland’s husband escapes burning boat after engine explodes 20 miles offshore
articles.summary: Kathy Ireland shared dramatic footage of husband Greg Olsen's boat engulfed in flames after an engine explosion 20 miles west of Santa Barbara.
articles.body: Kathy Ireland is thankful after her husband narrowly escaped a fire that engulfed his boat while he was alone at sea. In a recent Instagram post, the 63-year-old actress shared video of husband Dr. Greg Olsen's boat, the 4th Watch, engulfed in flames. Ireland said Olsen was out alone on the water while she was away on business. "Life is really hard and really beautiful. God is great," she wrote. "Engine exploded and a fire quickly melted all navigation equipment and survival raft!" She then thanked everyone "who prayed and continue to pray" for her husband, as well as all "those who aided in the rescue," including "@towboatus_ventura and the entire community" for their quick response. KATHY IRELAND REVEALS 'BIG RED FLAG' THAT EXPOSED ALLEGED $100M 'UNCONSCIONABLE' BETRAYAL "Most of all, we thank our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ for this miracle of his survival," she added. Ireland also shared a note she wrote to her husband following the incident, saying her "heart is both heavy and full" because she knows how much "love, sweat and life you poured into this vessel." "This vessel brought so much joy and so many blessings to our family and countless others," she continued. "My heart is heavy with yours. This is more than a boat, there are many implications. My heart is mostly full. Full because of the outpouring of love and support. Multitudes were praying for you! I’m so thankful to all who rushed to pray and come to your rescue." "I’m so thankful God gifted you with a brilliant mind to navigate this disaster so seamlessly," she added. "I’m eternally thankful to Him for loving and rescuing you. Though the vessel is no more, the 4th Watch is forever. You named that boat so profoundly. He has so much ahead for you! I’m so proud of you." WATCH: KATHY IRELAND SHARES THE LESSONS SHE'S LEARNED FROM WORKING AS A COMMERCIAL FISHERMAN Fans in the comments section shared well-wishes for Ireland and Olsen, with some recounting their own experiences with losing their belongings due to a fire. "Unbelievable!!! I’m SO grateful your husband is ok," one fan wrote. "🙏 And having parents who lost their home in a fire I completely understand your sadness about the loss of the boat. " "Oh my! I am so glad he is safe," another added. "The boat and gear is replaceable, but the emotions are real. So sorry!!!!" A third follower wrote, "So sorry to hear this, BUT, Thankful to God that he saved your Precious One!" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The TowBoatUS Ventura Instagram account also shared video of the fire and its aftermath, saying the company received a call about the fire around 3 p.m. on Wednesday afternoon, noting the vessel was "20 nautical miles west of Santa Barbara Harbor." In its post, TowBoatUS Ventura credited Olsen for his quick thinking, noting that he "was prepared and did everything right." They wrote that he initially "attempted to extinguish the fire before ultimately activating his EPIRB and abandoning ship into a kayak." "This was about as good an outcome as one could hope for in an otherwise serious emergency," the message read. "A well-prepared mariner, good samaritans nearby, and commercial vessels equipped and ready to respond made all the difference. It is a great reminder of the importance of preparedness, cooperation, and the maritime community looking out for one another." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: MC Hariel declara independência com o álbum 'Aplauso não paga as contas' | G1
articles.body:
MC Hariel afirma que revê a trajetória no funk ao longo das 13 faixas do álbum 'Aplauso não paga as contas' — Foto: Renan Miranda / Divulgação

♬ A caminho dos 29 anos, a serem festejados em 20 de dezembro, MC Hariel zera o jogo com a edição do álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”, em rotação nos aplicativos de áudio desde sexta-feira, 13 de dezembro.

Doze anos após ter ganhado projeção no universo do funk ao pôr em campo a música “Passei sorrindo” (2014), Haniel Denaro Ribeiro declara a independência artística.

O artista saiu da produtora GR6 após 12 anos e abriu a empresa Zaori em 2025 para gerir a própria carreira em sincronia com a gravadora que criou em 2024, Xaolin Records, selo fonográfico que Hariel mantém em associação com a Warner Music, companhia fonográfica que edita os lançamentos do artista desde 2021.

É essa gravadora que distribui no mercado digital o álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”, com o qual o MC paulistano afirma revisar a trajetória no universo do funk ao longo de 13 faixas gravadas com produção musical de nomes como André Nine, DJ Perera (colaborador de Hariel desde os tempos do já mencionado primeiro single de sucesso do artista, “Passei sorrindo”), Deejhay Luh, Ecologik, Fejuca, DK Kaio Mix, LT no Beat, Murilo e Pdrin.

O álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas” sucede o EP “A Vida é um Freestyle” (2026), lançado em 16 de abril como o primeiro movimento de independência de Hariel.

Com 15 anos de carreira iniciada de forma caseira em 2011, o MC agrega no álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas” os quatro participantes vitoriosos – MC Campos, MC Coutto, MC Dan e Kisha Zo – do concurso de freestyle que promoveu no embalo do lançamento do EP anterior.

Kisha Zo figura na faixa “Questão de tempo”. MC Campos & MC Dan unem vozes em “Só tá sem amor”. Já MC Coutto é o convidado de “Rakeada”.

“Eu vim da periferia e sei que existe muito talento ali, mas, muitas vezes, falta oportunidade para esse talento aparecer. Esse concurso foi uma forma de abrir uma porta para quem acompanha meu trabalho e sonha em viver de música, assim como eu sonhei um dia. Ver esses quatro fãs entrarem no estúdio, participarem do processo e terem suas faixas no álbum mostra que, quando a oportunidade é real, ela pode mudar caminhos”, argumenta Hariel no texto de apresentação do álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”.

MC Lkazin e Gblack, artistas da nova geração do elenco da produtora GR6, completam o time de convidados de MC Hariel no álbum, antecedido em 29 de outubro pela edição do single com a música “Outono”. Lkazin aparece na faixa “Maloqueiro e sonhador”. Já Gblack participa da música “Imaginando”.

Capa do álbum 'Aplauso não paga as contas', de MC Hariel — Foto: Renan Miranda / Divulgação

articles.title: Paulliny Tort: Livro Os Imortais terá filme de Rodrigo Teixeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Paulliny Tort conquistou prêmios nacionais com obra. História narra drama protagonizado por neandertais, e inclui um encontro com a espécie humana como conhecemos.
articles.summary: O premiado livro Os Imortais, de Paulliny Tort, será adaptado para o cinema pela RT Features, de Rodrigo Teixeira, mesmo produtor do sucesso Ainda Estou Aqui.
articles.body:
Paulliny Tort — Foto: Renato Parada/Divulgação

Após vencer o Prêmio Literário Biblioteca Nacional, a escritora brasiliense Paulliny Tort vai estrear no cinema com o romance Os Imortais (2026), publicado pela Editora Fósforo.

A obra será adaptada para o cinema pela RT Features, do premiado produtor Rodrigo Teixeira , um dos nomes responsáveis pela adaptação de "Ainda estou aqui" .

Em outubro, o livro – que narra o drama de um grupo de neandertais em busca de sobrevivência – venceu a premiação da Biblioteca Nacional na categoria romance.

🏆 Paulliny compartilha o prêmio com autores estreantes e nomes ilustres da literatura brasileira, como Adélia Prado, vencedora na categoria poesia, e Maria Valéria Rezende, em contos.

Nas redes sociais, a produtora contou que a obra já está em desenvolvimento.

A ideia começou do encantamento de Rodrigo pela obra.

“Eu fiquei maravilhado quando li este livro. Paulliny Tort entrega uma dimensão épica em cada palavra e, ao mesmo tempo, aborda questões universais sobre a humanidade, e isso torna esse projeto especialmente instigante para nós. Não poderíamos estar mais entusiasmados em levar essa história para o cinema", diz o produtor.

O cineasta afirma ainda que a obra consolida a trajetória da RT com adaptações literárias.

Uma das mais famosas é a versão de "Me chame pelo seu nome" (2017) . O livro, do escritor André Aciman, deu origem ao longa de 2017 protagonizado por Armie Hammer e Thimotée Chalamet e vencedor do Oscar de Melhor Roteiro Adaptado em 2018.

A produtora também encerrou, neste ano, as gravações de "Zero K" , adaptação do romance homônimo do americano Don DeLillo. E se prepara para adaptar "Não fossem as sílabas do sábado" , da brasileira Mariana Salomão Carrara.

"É um romance extraordinário em muitos sentidos, e a adaptação terá o desafio, mas também o privilégio, de manejar essas particularidades a favor do formado audiovisual. Tenho certeza de que o Rodrigo Teixeira e a equipe da RT são os parceiros ideais para essa empreitada, pela combinação perfeita que eles fazem entre ousadia e sensibilidade", destacou Rita Mattar, sócia-fundadora da editora.

Passada no período de surgimento da espécie humana como conhecemos, ' Os Imortais' narra a história na perspectiva do Homem, um neandertal que chefia o próprio grupo na luta por sobrevivência .

Em meio a caçadas e confrontos para garantir a segurança da própria espécie, o personagem é atravessado pelo luto pelos que ficam no caminho e o medo do desconhecido.

O ponto de virada da história ocorre quando o grupo de neandertais encontram uma comunidade de outros seres humanos, mas com formas físicas e hábitos que causam estranhamento pelas diferenças. As espécies coexistiram há cerca de 40 mil anos.

“Eu costumo dizer que eu não fiz uma pesquisa para o livro. Mesmo antes da universidade, mesmo quando eu era criança, adolescente, eu já lia sobre. Daí, quando eu chego para escrever uma história, tem esse background”, conta a escritora.

“Todo o esforço da literatura é sobre a experiência de estar vivo, o que a gente sente diante da experiência de estar vivo. A experiência da vida impacta não só nós, pessoas. Então, seja um neandertal, ou seja um grupo de crianças em situação de rua como Jorge Amado [em 'Capitães de areia'], ou mesmo uma autoficção, ele sempre vai passar por esses sentimentos, esses estranhamentos, os encantamentos da vida”, afirma.

Um dos desafios da adaptação para as telas deve ser a linguagem — ou a falta dela.

No livro, a "não palavra" está presente nos olhares e gestos das personagens, que se comunicam sem precisar dizer. Afinal, a linguagem como conhecemos só seria criada depois.

"Tem um autor que eu gosto muito [Steven Pinker], que traz vários exemplos de como a nossa mente funciona em duas frentes. Pensamento e linguagem são coisas entrelaçadas, mas que evoluem separadamente. Se o pensamento carecesse de linguagem para existir, nunca existiriam palavras novas", pontua.

Para a escritora, as obras surgem de uma cena, a partir da qual ela desenvolve sem saber no que vai dar. Em "Os imortais", a imagem foi a de um neandertal caçando um javali.

“Eu sentei, comecei a trabalhar, gostei da imagem. Fui ficando, fui me envolvendo com o personagem. E aos poucos, ele foi me apresentando o resto da história”, contou ao g1.

Os Imortais, de Paulliny Tort. Editora Fósforo, 2026. — Foto: Divulgação

“Eu escrevo com o prazer da descoberta, eu quero saber aonde a história vai me levar. Às vezes, eu até sei aonde ela vai me levar, mas não como ela vai me levar. Quando eu estou escrevendo, eu posso até saber o que vai acontecer, mas não sei como, vou descobrir escrevendo”, afirma.

✍️ Mas a escrita não é feita de um “momento de inspiração”.

A autora destaca que a escrita tem uma série de ferramentas. É necessário estudar temas, ler referências, assistir coisas novas e tudo aquilo que estimule a criação.

Atualmente, Paulliny se dedica exclusivamente à escrita e defende o reconhecimento da profissão.

“Todas as linguagens artísticas merecem um status de trabalho. A gente tem que tratar essas pessoas com dignidade na sociedade, porque o que elas oferecem para a gente é precioso também”, pontua.

Para a escritora, a literatura brasileira vive um momento de “menos timidez” . Há um movimento de maior interesse dos leitores e mais procura de escritores para publicação.

Segundo levantamento feito pela Câmara Brasileira do Livro, o Brasil ganhou 3 milhões de leitores entre 2024 e 2025.

“A visibilidade para a literatura contemporânea aumentou, a gente tem clubes de leitura, tem esse movimento de ler mulheres, que eu acho que também ajudou muito. Não só mulheres, mas, por exemplo, o Itamar [Vieira Junior], que é um fenômeno da literatura nacional, tem revistas especializadas. Então, eu acho que tem gente querendo ler autores e autoras brasileiras cada vez mais”, comenta.

A tendência, aponta a autora, é que esse número cresça ainda mais. Para isso, no entanto, Paulliny defende que haja políticas de incentivo.

Uma das ações é o MEC Livros, iniciativa do Ministério da Educação que dá acesso a livros digitais de forma gratuita. Paulliny comenta que o projeto ainda apresenta uma série de fatores a serem melhorados, como a remuneração de autores e os processos de seleção das obras, mas é um passo importante.

“Existem diferentes tipos de livros para diferentes tipos de pessoas. O importante é que existam políticas públicas para o livro e para a leitura, isso eu acho que é indispensável”, finaliza.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' box office collection day 10: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film earns over 3 times 'Animal'; crosses Rs 1,200 cr worldwide; Hindi version leads
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second Saturday. The mythological epic collected Rs 72.90 cr net in India on Day 10, registering a 51.6% rise over the previous day's earnings. With this, the film's domestic net collection has reached Rs 685.60 cr, while its India gross stands at Rs 819.50 cr. The film has also crossed the Rs 1,200 cr milestone worldwide, with its cumulative gross collection reaching Rs 1,228 cr.Ramayana Movie Review'Ramayana' Day 10 box office collection across languagesAccording to Sacnilk, the Hindi version remained the biggest contributor to the film's Saturday earnings. It collected Rs 53.75 cr from 18,557 shows. The Kannada version followed with Rs 5.40 cr from 893 screenings. Both Malayalam and Tamil versions earned Rs 4.75 cr each, from 1,127 and 1,290 shows, respectively. Telugu contributed another Rs 4.25 cr through 1,584 screenings.Across all five languages, the film registered an overall occupancy of 45.5% on Saturday. Malayalam recorded the highest occupancy at 83%, followed by Tamil at 62.5% and Kannada at 58.8%. Hindi registered 41.9%, while Telugu recorded 39.1%.For the Hindi 3D version, overall occupancy stood at 53%. Morning shows recorded 30.08%, while afternoon screenings reached 57.08%. Evening shows registered 62.77% occupancy, followed by 62.08% during the night.'Ramayana' worldwide box office collection crosses Rs 1,200 crThe film's overseas performance has further strengthened its global box office position. International markets contributed Rs 30 cr on Day 10, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 408.50 cr. Combined with its domestic gross, the worldwide collection has reached Rs 1,228 cr, according to Sacnilk.The domestic market accounts for 66.7% of the worldwide earnings, while overseas territories contribute the remaining 33.3%. The film's average collection per show on Saturday was Rs 32,454. Its latest performance also marks a considerable improvement over Friday, when it earned Rs 48.10 cr net in India.'Ramayana' box office collection: Day-wise performance'Ramayana' began its theatrical journey on November 5 with Rs 64.85 cr net in India. After collecting Rs 48.05 cr on Friday, the film recovered on Saturday with Rs 69.80 cr. Sunday brought in Rs 56.15 cr before Monday delivered its biggest single-day collection of Rs 107.50 cr.The film subsequently earned Rs 94.10 cr on Tuesday and Rs 70.65 cr on Wednesday. Its first Thursday collection stood at Rs 53.50 cr. The opening eight-day run generated Rs 564.60 cr net and Rs 675.05 cr gross domestically.Friday's earnings during the second week stood at Rs 48.10 cr. Saturday's improved performance pushed the two-day second-week total to Rs 121 cr net and Rs 144.45 cr gross. The Hindi version has contributed Rs 527.25 cr to the domestic net collection so far, accounting for 76.9% of the total. Kannada follows with Rs 57.35 cr, while Telugu has generated Rs 44.90 cr. Tamil and Malayalam have contributed Rs 29.65 cr and Rs 26.45 cr, respectively.Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' earns over three times 'Animal'The latest figures also put the film ahead of Ranbir Kapoor's previous release, 'Animal', at the same stage of its theatrical run. Directed by Sandeep Reddy Vanga, the action drama collected Rs 36 cr net in India on its tenth day. This is less than half of 'Ramayana's' corresponding domestic earnings.'Animal' recorded Rs 33.53 cr from its Hindi version, with 12,949 shows. Telugu contributed Rs 2.13 cr through 1,168 screenings, while Tamil added Rs 30 lakh from 222 shows. Kannada and Malayalam each earned Rs 2 lakh, from 17 and 34 screenings, respectively.By Day 10, 'Animal' had accumulated Rs 431.27 cr net and Rs 514.05 cr gross in India. Its overseas gross stood at Rs 203.25 cr, including Rs 13.75 cr from the tenth day. The worldwide gross collection reached Rs 717.30 cr. Its second-week earnings had reached Rs 93.69 cr, with the tenth day contributing Rs 36 cr.About 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend''Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' brings the timeless Indian epic about Lord Rama and King Ravana to the screen through a contemporary cinematic adaptation. The story has influenced generations and remains deeply rooted in India's cultural traditions.The first instalment focuses on Prince Rama's early life and the challenges he encounters as the rightful heir to Ayodhya. Headlined by Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, the ambitious film revisits the legendary narrative through modern Indian cinema.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. All figures are approximate unless explicitly mentioned, offering a fair representation of the movie's box office performance. These totals may change as official studio data is updated or as additional international market reports are finalized. articles.title: Kristin Cavallari makes steamy bedroom confession ahead of 40th birthday
articles.summary: Kristin Cavallari revealed intimate details about her sex life on her "Let's Be Honest" podcast as she looks ahead to her upcoming 40th birthday.
articles.body: Kristin Cavallari is giving fans an inside look at what goes on in her bedroom in a steamy confession on her podcast. In a recent episode of her "Let's Be Honest" podcast, the 39-year-old reality star opened up about her upcoming 40th birthday and gave some insight into her sex life, noting she isn't having sex but says: "Your sex drive as you get older is like wild." "Like age 40, I'm way more sexual than I was at 25. Again, it would be nice if I had an outlet for it, but we can have sex with ourselves, which is what I f---ing do all the time," she said. "But that's one of the reasons why I can't wait to be in a relationship is I feel like I've become this like sexual being." She explained that her last relationship "was a very sexual relationship," but that that was something she needed, and admits it is something she misses. KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION Cavallari added that she is now looking forward to turning 40, saying, "If this is what 40s is, like f- - - yeah. This is fun." Earlier in the episode, the "Very Cavallari" star quipped that it "takes one to two years of abstinence to become a nun" and that she is on her way towards that achievement. The reality star was previously married to former professional football quarterback Jay Cutler from 2013 to 2020, when she announced they were getting a divorce. They share three children; Camden, 14, Jaxon, 12, and Saylor, 10. When speaking about her divorce, on the "Aspire with Emma Grede" podcast in July 2026, the "Laguna Beach" star claimed she gained the confidence to leave her marriage because of the success of her company, Uncommon James. I had to give him half the value of Uncommon James in cash and properties and everything else. Yeah. Isn't that interesting?" Following her divorce, she dated Mark Estes for a few months in 2024 and country singer Morgan Wallen. She told Bunnie XO on the "Dumb Blonde" podcast in December 2024 that Wallen "was good in bed." "I'll be honest with you. He was the first guy in my f---ing life that wasn’t just completely enamored with me ... It really threw me," she said. articles.title: Parenting advice by Khloé Kardashian: 'It's so important for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit,' reveals the diva, explaining how she stopped her daughter from quitting gymnastics
articles.summary: Discover how Khloé Kardashian inspired her daughter True to keep pursuing gymnastics despite struggles, emphasizing the importance of showing kids that even adults can fail and learn.
articles.body: Khloé Kardashian wasn't about to let her daughter give up gymnastics over one cartwheel. True, who is eight, was frustrated because she couldn't nail the move, and she kept comparing herself to her cousins, who seemed to be doing much better. So Khloé came up with a plan. She'd try a cartwheel herself, fully expecting to fail at it too.She told the story on an episode of her podcast, Khloé in Wonder Land, with actor Goldie Hawn as her guest. They were discussing parenting and kids' confidence, and Khloé described how her own clumsy attempt ended up changing True's mind.Why did True Thompson want to quit gymnastics?According to Khloé Kardashian, True was thinking about giving up because her cousins could do the cartwheel better than she could. It was really getting to her, especially watching the other kids manage something she was stuck on.So Khloé said she'd go to gymnastics and try as well. She wanted True to see that even grown-ups can't do everything, and that nothing is embarrassing about that. Here's how she remembered putting it to her daughter: "Girl, do you want to? Okay. I'm going to go to gymnastics with you. I'm going to do a cartwheel because I can't do one. And I'm going to show her that an adult can't do this. And you're going to be fine."Khloé Kardashian's cartwheel attempt made True more confidentShe did go through with it, and it sounds like it didn't go to plan. She was laughing about it on the podcast, saying, "So I did a cartwheel the best I could. It was silly. I looked ridiculous."That was enough to make True feel better about her own effort. Watching her mum struggle with the same move made her realise she wasn't as bad at it as she'd thought.And it worked. Khloé Kardashian said True kept going with gymnastics for another three years after that. In her words: "She now has been in gymnastics three years longer because she saw how ridiculous I looked and she looked way better than me. So she has all this confidence."Khloé Kardashian on why parents should let children see them failThe chat with Goldie Hawn moved on to why parents don't need to look perfect in front of their children. Khloé Kardashian thinks kids should see adults mess up and, just as importantly, see what they do next. She said, "It's so important, I think, for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit. Like, how do we handle that?"The gymnastics story is a pretty good example. She didn't give True another pep talk about trying harder. She just made herself the example, couldn't do the cartwheel either, and was happy to laugh at herself about it.Khloé Kardashian says daughter True won't get social media anytime soonKhloé Kardashian also talked about the rules she's set around phones and social media. True is eight and doesn't have a phone, and Khloé has no plans to let her on social media any time soon. "My daughter's only eight, but she's not getting social media for a very long time. She doesn't even have a phone," she said.She also sounded a bit baffled by how young some kids are when they get their first phone. "Kids these days have phones at eight. I'm like, who are you calling? I don't understand," she added.Khloé shares True and her four-year-old son, Tatum Thompson, with her ex Tristan Thompson. She's talked about different parts of raising the two of them before, and this time it was one small moment from True's gymnastics classes that came up.Khloé didn't get the cartwheel, but True got something out of watching her try. She stuck with gymnastics, and her mum came away with a pretty funny story.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Blake Lively’s beverage venture winds down after five years; sales concerns emerge amid Justin Baldoni legal battle - Reports
articles.summary: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture.
articles.body: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture. The company operates Betty Buzz, a non-alcoholic beverage brand, and its alcoholic counterpart, Betty Booze. Recent developments surrounding the business have raised questions about its future, including inactive social media accounts and changes to its trademark portfolio.According to PEOPLE, the company is winding down its operations and is expected to cease business. The Betty Buzz website is no longer accessible, while the Betty Booze website remained operational as of November 10. The latter continues to showcase its products, although the overall status of the business remains unclear.The reported development follows a series of changes involving the company's online presence and intellectual property filings. While these developments have fuelled speculation about a possible shutdown, the available reports alone do not confirm that the business has officially closed.Beverage venture face uncertain futureBlake Lively launched the beverage venture with two distinct product lines. Both brands were introduced as part of the actress's move into the consumer products market.However, the company's digital presence has changed considerably. The Betty Buzz website is now unavailable, while Betty Booze continues to maintain an active website. The difference has attracted attention amid reports that the business is preparing to wind down.PEOPLE reported that the company is expected to stop operating. Neither the continued availability of the Betty Booze website nor the status of its products necessarily indicates that the brand will remain in business.Several trademark applications abandonedTMZ reported on November 4 that multiple trademark applications associated with Blake Lively's beverage company had been abandoned. The filings were made after the business was launched and covered several categories of products.These included beer-based beverages, non-alcoholic carbonated drinks and other products. However, the trademarks for Betty Buzz and Betty Booze remain active, according to the report.For the unversed, abandoned applications do not automatically mean that a company has ceased operations. Likewise, active registrations for the two principal brands do not establish whether their products will continue to be sold.Instagram accounts show reduced activityThe company's social media presence has also become less frequent. Betty Booze's Instagram account last published an update on September 28, 2026. Betty Buzz's account has been inactive since April 5, 2026.The lack of recent posts, combined with the Betty Buzz website becoming inaccessible, has prompted further questions about the brands' operations. Justin Baldoni legal battle draws attentionThe reported wind-down comes amid Blake Lively's ongoing legal dispute with actor-director Justin Baldoni, her co-star in 'It Ends With Us'. The case has generated considerable public attention, and the negative publicity surrounding the actress is believed to have affected the beverage business.An internal document that became public during the legal proceedings reportedly showed significant sales declines for both Betty Buzz and Betty Booze in August 2024. The figures highlighted the commercial difficulties faced by the brands during that period.According to Inc., retail buyers had also expressed concerns about the potential impact of the controversy surrounding Lively on the beverage lines. While the extent of the damage to sales remains unclear, the reported concerns suggest that the publicity became a factor in how retailers viewed the business.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Former DC head James Gunn shuts down 'Man of Tomorrow' editing rumours, says no Skydance executive has seen the film: 'Any stories around this narrative are false'
articles.summary: James Gunn refutes rumors that Skydance executives demanded changes to the upcoming Superman sequel 'Man of Tomorrow', confirming they haven't seen the film yet.
articles.body: James Gunn has pushed back on rumours about his upcoming DC film 'Man of Tomorrow'. Reports had been circulating that Skydance executives watched the Superman sequel and asked for big changes, but Gunn says that simply isn’t true. As he put it, no one from the company has seen the movie yet, so there’s been no screening and no notes.Gunn addressed the discussion in a post on Threads on November 13, following the announcement that he and Peter Safran would step away from their leadership positions at DC Studios. The news raised questions among fans about the future of projects developed under their management, particularly the next chapter of Superman's story.“There are a lot of untrue rumours going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen ‘Man of Tomorrow’ and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made,” Gunn wrote.“No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false. ”What rumours surrounded 'Man of Tomorrow'?Speculation about the film intensified after reports suggested that the incoming studio leadership could request significant changes to Gunn's sequel. Online discussions included claims about possible reshoots, removed character appearances, and changes to the filmmaker's creative control.Some of the rumours also raised questions about the involvement of characters connected to the wider DC Universe, including Supergirl and Blue Beetle. However, these claims were not confirmed by DC Studios or Skydance.Gunn's response specifically addressed the suggestion that Skydance executives had already watched the film and ordered a major overhaul. By saying who has actually seen the film, Gunn shot down that narrative. He didn’t promise anything about future studio decisions, but he did push back on claims that executives had already stepped into the editing process.Why are James Gunn and Peter Safran leaving DC Studios?The rumours surfaced at a significant time for DC Studios. Big news landed on November 9: Skydance announced that Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts after four years in charge of the division. They’ll officially be out on December 1, 2026. Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer. He will oversee the studio's film, television and animation projects and report to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein.In its official announcement, Skydance said Gunn and Safran would return full-time to their creative work. Gunn and Safran also said they still want to keep telling stories they care about, including the next chapter of Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story in 'Man of Tomorrow'.Their departure from executive positions does not mean they are leaving the film behind. Gunn remains its writer and director, while he and Safran are attached as producers.What is 'Man of Tomorrow' about?'Man of Tomorrow' is the follow-up to Gunn’s 2025 film 'Superman'. It continues Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story, with the two rivals teaming up against a bigger threat. David Corenswet returns as Superman, and Nicholas Hoult is back as Lex Luthor.The film also introduces Lars Eidinger as Brainiac, a major antagonist from DC Comics. Rachel Brosnahan is returning as Lois Lane, alongside other familiar faces from the previous film.The production completed principal photography in August 2026, with Gunn confirming the wrap through his social media. The film is now in post-production and is scheduled to arrive in theatres on July 9, 2027, according to the official announcement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Black women's swimming documentary Swim Sistas Oscar-longlisted
articles.summary: Cat White says it is "just the most beautiful feeling" to see her film so well received.
articles.body:
The director of a documentary that honours the "powerful celebration of black British women's relationship with water" has been longlisted for an Oscar.

Cat White, from Northampton, said the 11-minute film Swim Sistas could make it to the final nominations for the Best Documentary Short Film at the 99th Academy Awards.

She said it was "just the most beautiful feeling" to see it so well received.

It features Jasmine Boatswain , also from the town, who appeared in the second series of Traitors. She said it was "insane" that an uplifting film about freedom and women's empowerment was getting so much attention.

The film took a day to shoot with a budget of £5,000 and was narrated by the Oscar-nominated actor Naomie Harris.

It also features Alice Dearing, the first black woman to represent Team GB in swimming at an Olympic Games, athlete Lexi Sandiford and Roni Bruno who learned to swim at 54.

White said the film was a tiny idea that was a true "labour of love". It grew from her love of early morning swimming during the Covid-19 pandemic after she suffered a double bereavement.

She said: "I found that the water gave me a sense of peace and healing in a time where it was kind of impossible to get that closure."

She said a further reason to make the film was that Swim England statistics showed about 5% of black adults in the United Kingdom regularly swim.

"It just completely stopped me in my tracks and I began to ask what would it look like if more people who look like me could experience this joy that I get from the water and I built this community around me", she added.

"What better way to change the narrative than by putting them in a film and telling the world about them?"

The film has won several awards including Best Documentary at Northampton Film Festival. It was also the Jury's Choice Award at the Academy Award-qualifying Thomas Edison Film Festival, Best Documentary at the BAFTA and BIFA-qualifying Women X Film Festival and Best Short Film at Kendal Mountain Festival.

It also featured at the inaugural United Nations Swimmable Cities Summit in Rotterdam and was being incorporated into the French national curriculum.

Boatswain said making the film with her family friend was "really special".

She said: "It's a film about breaking outside of the binary - I guess the box you've been put into."

As well as being a swimming enthusiast, Boatswain also used to play rugby for Old Northamptonians and was "the only girl on the rugby team".

She said: "When I tell people that I can swim, that I enjoy the water and going on holiday and jumping out into the sea, people seem quite shocked [and say] 'Oh you can do that' - yes I can.

"I never thought that I'd be involved in anything in my life that would be Oscar adjacent, it's incredible."

She added that White had an "absolutely brilliant mind".

White said it was a "massive boost" that Wunmi Mosaku , who won a BAFTA for Damiola, A Loved Boy and was Oscar-nominated for Sinners, had now joined her as an executive producer.

"I'm developing the project into a wider series where we explore stories around the world, Africa, the Caribbean, the US, black women's stories with water, but I'm interested in Asian women's stories with water, men's stories with water."

She said at a screening in New York someone came up to her and said they had been inspired to "go and learn to swim - which brought it all home".

articles.title: Bowen Yang returns to ‘SNL’ to play ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Former “Saturday Night Live” repertory player and writer Bowen Yang returned to help open the show this weekend with his portrayal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
articles.body: Former “Saturday Night Live” repertory player and writer Bowen Yang returned to help open the show this weekend with his portrayal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. In the cold open, the nation’s most-prominent tech-industry CEOs, including Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, are at a CIA gathering devised to teach them how to identify when a woman may be duping them. “America needs you to learn the difference between a woman who would actually want to have sex with you and a woman who is clearly a spy,” said a CIA guide, portrayed by comedian John Mulaney, the night’s host. Mulaney, a former “SNL” writer, used the story of Huang, who resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following reports that he had extramarital relationships, including one with a suspected spy for China. “What do you think the lesson is here?” Mulaney asked. Zuckerberg, portrayed by Andrew Dismukes, answered: “Never date a human woman.” Mulaney dismissed the response and that of a few of the other tech titans in the room, prompting PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel, portrayed by James Austin Johnson, to defend the group. “Show us some respect,” he said. “We do a lot for this country. Name one time technology has let us down.” Mulaney answered by mentioning Friday’s nationwide flight ground stop and Thursday’s global Microsoft glitch. He tried to empathize, however, noting that it’s a rare time in human history when men “as pale and as strange as you” even survive, let alone possess “all the world’s wealth and power.” Mulaney asked the group to remember the people they dated before they were rich and famous. “Now all of a sudden someone very beautiful is interested in you. Why do you think that might be?” he said. Zuckerberg chimed in. “Because she’s comforted by my Meta glasses recording her at all times.” “No,” Mulaney said. He later introduces someone “who learned this lesson the hard way.” Enter Huang. “It’s me, Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang,” Yang said. He explained that he’s into BDSM — “breakin’ da stock market” — and urged the men not to be like him. “Women don’t like guys like us,” he said. “That’s how we became guys like us.” Yang appeared in a subsequent sketch, “Little Park of Horrors,” a spoof of Broadway musicals, that centered on the city outlawing horse-drawn carriages and the two men (Marcello Hernández and Kam Patterson) who want to ride in one. Eventually realizing the dangers and limitations, the pair opt for a vehicle ride in the Lincoln Tunnel only to be confronted by Yang’s Mary Todd Lincoln, who sang about the pitfalls of such a subterranean journey. “No way it’s taking less than two hours,” Lincoln sang. “ ... And it won’t be for free. I’m sayin,’ I’m sayin’ that you and you and you — you’re going to pay me.” A fan favorite, Yang started as a writer in 2018 and joined the cast the next year. He left “SNL” in December 2025, and made his Broadway debut in September as Lincoln in playwright Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!” The night’s musical guest was Phoebe Bridgers. “SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend': Nitesh Tiwari responds to criticism of Sai Pallavi's action scenes as Sita; cites 'Adbhuta Ramayana' and 'Bilanka Ramayana'
articles.summary: Director Nitesh Tiwari has responded to the criticism surrounding Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita in 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'.
articles.body: Director Nitesh Tiwari has responded to the criticism surrounding Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita in 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'. The actress's action sequences have triggered discussions, with some viewers questioning the creative decision to present the mythological character as a warrior.Addressing the debate, Nitesh Tiwari has explained that his interpretation is based on lesser-known versions of the Ramayana. He cited ancient and regional literary traditions that describe Sita as a powerful manifestation of divine energy. However, actor Mukesh Khanna has expressed a contrasting opinion, arguing that the portrayal does not align with his understanding of the character.Nitesh Tiwari explains the inspiration behind warrior SitaIn an interview with The Federal, Nitesh Tiwari discussed the references that influenced his approach to Sita's character. He pointed towards the Sanskrit text 'Adbhuta Ramayana' and the 15th-century Odia work 'Bilanka Ramayana'. According to the filmmaker, these versions present Sita differently from the familiar depiction of her as a figure defined primarily by endurance and sacrifice.“These tellings offer a rather different image of Sita: not merely a figure of endurance but an active warrior and an embodiment of cosmic Shakti.”The director explained that these literary traditions provided the foundation for portraying Sita with a more active role in the battle against evil. He maintained that the interpretation was not an entirely new concept introduced for modern audiences.Sita takes Mahakali's form to defeat Sahasra RavanaNitesh Tiwari further referred to an episode in which Sita transforms into Mahakali to confront Sahasra Ravana, a thousand-headed demon king. The narrative describes the incident taking place when Rama is incapacitated and unable to defeat the powerful adversary himself.“In these versions, she assumes the fierce form of Mahakali and slays Sahasra Ravana, the thousand-headed demon king, when Rama is incapacitated,” he said.Mukesh Khanna criticises Sai Pallavi's action sequencesMeanwhile, actor Mukesh Khanna has questioned the decision to show Sai Pallavi performing action sequences as Sita. He argued that the character's traditional representation should not be altered to accommodate contemporary interpretations. Interestingly, the actor clarified that he had not watched the movie. His reaction was based on discussions and reviews circulating on social media.As quoted by Kerala Kaumudi, Mukesh Khanna said, "To the best of my knowledge, Valmiki's Ramayana does not mention Sita fighting in a battle anywhere. Sita, the wife of Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram, was a symbol of devotion and sacrifice."'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. The ensemble cast also includes Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sonakshi Sinha morphed photos case: Mumbai court holds Delhi arrest illegal, says, 'The record does not disclose satisfactory compliance'
articles.summary: A Mumbai court on Saturday freed a man who was picked up in Delhi over the alleged circulation of morphed nude pictures of actor Sonakshi Sinha.
articles.body: A Mumbai court on Saturday freed a man who was picked up in Delhi over the alleged circulation of morphed nude pictures of actor Sonakshi Sinha. The magistrate at the Bandra court held that the arrest was illegal because police did not follow the required legal steps while bringing him to Mumbai.Case filed after actor’s complaintAccording to the India Today report, the case was registered on Friday at Bandra police station in Mumbai. Sonakshi Sinha had complained that a person based in Delhi had shared doctored images of her on social media.Arrest in Delhi and journey to MumbaiThe accused, named as Aryan Deepak Jain, was taken into custody at about 10.11 am on Saturday from Jagatpuri Police Station in Delhi’s Shahdara area. He was then flown to Mumbai and presented before a magistrate at the Bandra court. The magistrate, however, ordered his release.Court flags lapse in procedureThe court noted that Aryan Deepak Jain was not first produced before the nearest magistrate in Delhi before being taken out of that jurisdiction. It observed:"Thus, it appears that the police have directly brought the accused from Delhi before this Court without following the procedure of production before the nearest Magistrate,” the court observed.The court also said the investigators had given no satisfactory reason for skipping this step.Police wanted three days of custodyBandra police had asked for three days of custody. They said they needed time to find the device or medium used to create the morphed image and to take the probe forward.Defence opposes custodyAryan Deepak Jain’s lawyers, Aman Shahi, Prashant Trivedi and Aditya Jain, strongly objected. They argued that the arrest broke mandatory safeguards, as police had neither served a notice nor told him the grounds for his arrest. They added that he was brought to Mumbai by air without being presented before a local magistrate.The defence also claimed the police acted in unusual haste because of the complainant’s influential position. Jain maintained that he had committed no offence and that the sections applied in the case did not prima facie fit the facts.Safeguards under BNSS not metThe magistrate observed that the offences carry a jail term of up to seven years. The court said:“Therefore, the investigating officer was required to comply with the safeguards under Section 35(1)(b) of the BNSS, including recording the reasons showing the necessity of arrest. The record does not disclose satisfactory compliance with the said requirement,” the court said.The court further made it clear that a need to investigate cannot alone justify an arrest.“The mere requirement of further investigation cannot, by itself, justify arrest and detention without following the statutory safeguards,” the court observed.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection day 11 (LIVE): Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash starrer crosses Rs 700 crore in India, expected to beat Dhurandhar's second Sunday number
articles.summary: ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ has had a remarkable first week at the box office and the film is on a winning streak, on its way to break several records.
articles.body: ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ has had a remarkable first week at the box office and the film is on a winning streak, on its way to break several records. The film achieved a series of milestones within its first seven days, including the biggest-ever Monday collection for a Hindi film, followed by record performances on Tuesday and Wednesday.As per Sacnilk, the film concluded its first week on Thursday, November 12, with an India collection of Rs 564 crore. Its impressive run continued on the eighth day, when it earned Rs 53.50 crore, followed by Rs 48 crore on Friday. The film witnessed a significant jump on its second Saturday, collecting Rs 72.90 crore. With the second weekend in progress, the numbers are expected to rise further as evening and night shows contribute to the overall collection.The film has already collected Rs 31.40 crore net through advance bookings for Sunday, day 11 putting it ahead of the entire day 11 collection of 'Dhurandhar' even before spot bookings and walk-ins are taken into account. This puts the second Sunday records of 'Jawan', 'Stree 2' and 'Dhurandhar 2' under considerable pressure. With 11.49 lakh tickets sold at an average ticket price of Rs 326, 'Ramayana' has already secured Rs 31.40 crore net before the first show. It now needs approximately Rs 31.61 crore from spot bookings and walk-ins through the day to surpass 'Dhurandhar 2's second Sunday record of Rs 63 crore.As of now, till afternoon, on day 11, which is its second Sunday, 'Ramayana' has collected Rs 34.26 crore till afternoon. The total collection of the film stands at Rs 719.86 crore in India. At the worldwide box office, the film has made Rs 1228 crore.Day wise collection of 'Ramayana: Part 1'Day 1 (Thursday) - Rs 64.85 croreDay 2 (Friday) - Rs 48.05 croreDay 3 (Saturday) - Rs 69.80 croreDay 4 (Sunday) - Rs 56.15 croreDay 5 (Monday) - Rs 107.50 croreDay 6 (Tuesday) - Rs 94.10 croreDay 7 (Wednesday) - Rs 70.65 croreDay 8 (Thursday) - Rs 53.50 croreDay 9 (Friday) - Rs 48.10 croreDay 10 (Saturday) - Rs 72.90 croreDay 11 (Sunday) LIVE - Rs 34.26 croreTotal net collection in India - Rs 719.86 croreGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Thalapathy Vijay's 'Ghilli' co-star Nancy Jennifer marries Karthik at 36; Viral wedding videos show traditional Hindu ceremony
articles.summary: Actress Nancy Jennifer, fondly remembered as Bhuvana from Vijay's blockbuster 'Ghilli', has entered a new phase of her personal life.
articles.body: Actress Nancy Jennifer, fondly remembered as Bhuvana from Vijay's blockbuster 'Ghilli', has entered a new phase of her personal life. The actress married Karthik in a traditional wedding ceremony on Sunday, November 15. Pictures and videos from the celebrations have circulated on social media, drawing attention from Tamil cinema fans. Though she had left movies, she was still adored by her fans because of her characters she played as a kid. Her wedding has now brought her back into the spotlight, with fans and well-wishers congratulating the couple.Nancy Jennifer's 'Ghilli' role as Vijay's sister Bhuvana made her popularNancy Jennifer first appeared as a child artiste in the 1997 film 'Nerukku Ner', featuring Vijay and Suriya. She also appeared in films such as 'Thayagam' and 'Ulavu Thurai' alongside Vijayakanth. Nevertheless, the character of Bhuvana in Dharani's 'Ghilli' as Vijay's younger sister made her very popular amongst Tamil moviegoers. The loving name 'Arisimootai' that Vijay gave her character was very well loved by fans.Nancy Jennifer's wedding videos show traditional Hindu marriage ritualsThe marriage took place at a beach resort on Chennai's East Coast Road in a traditional Hindu marriage ceremony. Videos of Karthik tying the mangalsutra around Nancy's neck have gone viral on social media. Their wedding also caught attention because Nancy is a Christian, while Karthik is a Hindu. The actress participated in the Hindu marriage ceremonies, and the visuals sparked discussion. Several social media posts congratulate the couple.Nancy Jennifer's career after 'Ghilli' and her business journeyAfter 'Ghilli', Nancy Jennifer acted in films like 'February 14', 'Unakkum Enakkum', 'Jambhavan', 'Thozha', 'Theeya Velai Seiyyanum Kumaru', 'Koottathil Oruthan' and 'Trip'. She even ventured into television but eventually left acting.In recent times, she has been involved in entrepreneurship through her business venture called Nature's Joy, which produces chemical-free products. Nancy was unmarried until now and has often spoken about her life outside of acting. Her marriage at the age of 36 is a special occasion for her fans who saw her on screen in 'Ghilli'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ram Gopal Varma backs Namit Malhotra's strategy for 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' and predicts: 'Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana Part 1'
articles.summary: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has once again praised ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, and this time he has also defended the money plan of producer Namit
articles.body: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has once again praised ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, and this time he has also defended the money plan of producer Namit Malhotra. In a long post on X, RGV said the film’s theatrical run is so strong that the first part alone may cover the cost of both instalments. He also predicted that the sequel will perform far better.Ram Gopal Varma shares a story about his motherRam Gopal Varma opened his post with a personal story. He said his mother never showed this kind of excitement even for his best films. He wrote, “Even for the best of my films, she didn’t do this, but my mother has been buying tickets for Namit Malhotra’s Ramayana for the servants, watchmen and others in the building complex where she lives.”According to RGV, this wave of excitement has helped the film break records. He believes it is moving towards becoming the “biggest hit ever in Indian cinematic history”. He has watched the film twice and had earlier called it the “Taj Mahal of cinema”.Ram Gopal Varma rejects the Rs 4,000 crore budget claimRam Gopal Varma said some people still argue that the film’s earnings are not enough. Their reasoning is that each of the two parts reportedly cost Rs 2,000 crore, which makes the total Rs 4,000 crore.The filmmaker does not agree with this figure. He claimed that the first part cost slightly less than Rs 800 crore. In his view, this amount already includes mutually beneficial deals, global tax benefits and subsidies, which will bring the cost down even further. He added that any reasonably experienced filmmaker can tell from watching the film that the cost could not have gone beyond this level.He also questioned the idea that both parts would need the same budget. He compared the two films to the two halves of one movie and wrote, “That’s like thinking the cost before the interval and after the interval will be the same in a film. I know of films where 50 per cent of the cost was just the climax.”Why does Ram Gopal Varma talk about ‘Pushpak vimaan’Ram Gopal Varma explained that a large share of the spending went into building the world of ‘Ramayana’. He said these creations will turn into assets that can be used again for the second film, gaming and other projects planned by Malhotra.According to him, most Bollywood filmmakers, trade analysts and self-styled experts do not understand this approach. Based on the current run, he predicted that the producer will get back the full cost of the first part, and possibly of both films, from the first instalment. After that, the earnings from digital and other non-theatrical rights of the first film, along with everything the sequel makes, would be added.Using an image from the epic, RGV joked that Namit Malhotra could then “build his own Pushpak vimaan”. He said the producer could invest in bold ventures that even the biggest production houses in north and south India have not tried. In time, he said, this could even help the producer overtake major Hollywood studios.RGV also took the names of Valmiki and Tulsidas while making a big claim about the producer. He wrote, “I don’t know what happened to Valmiki ji or Tulsidas ji after they did their work, but it is an irrefutable fact that, from now onwards, Namit Malhotra will be the biggest mega filmmaker in history since the May 3, 1913, release of Raja Harishchandra, up to whichever was the biggest film before November 5. If anyone has a doubt, just do the maths.”Why does he expect a bigger part 2The filmmaker said the second part will feature some of the story’s biggest moments. These include action scenes with Hanuman and the Vaanar Sena, Ram Sethu, the burning of Lanka, Sita in Lanka, the death of Kumbhakarna and the killing of Ravana.Ram Gopal Varma said Malhotra has shown a strong mix of strategy, business sense, creative understanding and vision. He compared the two ‘Ramayana’ films with the ‘KGF’ franchise and wrote, “If KGF 2 did around five times more than KGF 1, I am convinced that Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana Part 1. If you disagree, we will talk in 2028.”Second viewing adds to his praiseRam Gopal Varma had earlier said that he was just as impressed after seeing the film a second time. He described himself as an atheist and said he was judging the film as a lover of cinema, not as a devotee of Lord Ram.He praised the scale, ambition, visual effects and performances. In his opinion, some critics failed to see how the grand visuals add to the emotional effect of the story. He gave credit to director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra for trying something Indian cinema had never imagined before.This is not the first time he has backed the film. In an earlier post, he called it a powerful cinematic experience and asked the makers not to feel low because of poor reviews. He compared the criticism to “barking street dogs” when set against the effort that went into making the film.About the film and its castThe film is produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios along with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash plays Ravana and Ravie Dubey plays Lakshman. Sunny Deol will be seen as Lord Hanuman, who was introduced in the post-credits scene of the first part. Malhotra and Yash are also co-producers. The second part is expected to arrive on Diwali 2028.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: HBO revela en exclusiva una de las escenas de la serie de ‘Harry Potter’ más míticas de Hogwarts: cuenta con un detalle que no aparece en el libro
articles.standfirst: Un nuevo adelanto deja ver cómo será uno de los momentos más esperados del primer año de Harry
articles.summary: Un nuevo adelanto deja ver cómo será uno de los momentos más esperados del primer año de Harry
articles.body: No hace falta una Snitch dorada para atrapar la atención de los fans: a HBO le ha bastado un puñado de segundos. La serie de Harry Potter ha desvelado en exclusiva una de las escenas más queridas del primer libro, y lo ha hecho con un pequeño giro que ni los lectores más fieles de la saga esperaban. A falta de unas semanas para el estreno, la magia ya ha empezado a hacer efecto. El fragmento, compartido el sábado 14 de noviembre en la cuenta oficial de Harry Potter en Instagram, traslada al espectador al corazón de Hogwarts: el Gran Comedor durante el banquete de bienvenida. Tras la Ceremonia de Selección, los alumnos corean el nombre de Dumbledore y, como por arte de magia, las largas mesas se llenan de carne asada, verduras y postres dignos de Honeydukes. El decorado, levantado desde cero, recuerda mucho al de las películas, con sus mesas de madera, su luz cálida y sus muros de piedra. La auténtica sorpresa está en la mesa de los profesores. El Dumbledore de John Lithgow y la McGonagall de Janet McTeer mantienen una conversación que no aparece en la novela de J.K. Rowling, en la que la profesora comenta cuánto se parece Harry a su padre. Como el libro narra el banquete desde los ojos de Harry, este añadido abre una ventana a lo que piensan los adultos del castillo. El clip, además, funciona como un contrahechizo para las críticas: en el tráiler de septiembre, Harry y Ron aparecían ante un desayuno mucho más modesto, y algunos fans bromearon con la inflación en Hogwarts. Nada más publicarse el clip, las redes sociales se convirtieron en un auténtico Gran Comedor de opiniones, y muchos fans no tardaron en ponerlo frente a frente con la escena original de la película. Hubo quien elogió lo fiel que es la recreación del castillo y su ambiente, y quien celebró ver por fin conversaciones entre los profesores que las películas nunca mostraron. Si bien, las comparaciones siguen siendo odiosas. Hay quienes, han resaltado la falta de color y luz en esta escena mítica.

articles.title: Javed Akhtar spotted in wheelchair at Mumbai airport with Shabana Azmi, viral pics grab attention
articles.summary: Celebrated screenwriter and lyricist Javed Akhtar was spotted sitting in a wheelchair as he was captured by the shutterbugs with his wife and veteran
articles.body: Celebrated screenwriter and lyricist Javed Akhtar was spotted sitting in a wheelchair as he was captured by the shutterbugs with his wife and veteran actress Shabana Azmi at the Mumbai airport on Sunday.However, as the cameramen requested Javed Akhtar to pose while standing up, he obliged and faced the camera with Shabana Azmi.Shabana, who is extremely active on social media, keeps revisiting fond memories with her writer husband time and again.In October, the veteran actress recalled Javed Akhtar's difficult days, revealing how he battled extreme hardship before making a name for himself in the industry.Shabana shared that there were days when he had nowhere to sleep and barely had anything to eat.Dropping a rare throwback photo of Javed Akhtar on her official handle, Shabana Azmi wrote, "4th Oct 1964. A young lad arrived at Bombay Central Station with 27 naye paise in his pocket but with big dreams in his eyes. Life gave him several hard knocks. He slept on the footpaths, at the railway stations, and in the compound of many a studio. A day came when he had nothing to eat for 3 days and the only clothes he had were the shreds on his body.""On the edge of despair when he could have given up, he said to himself " Main yunhi marne ke liye nahin paida nahin hua tha . Yeh din badlenge ".. as they did . 4th October 1964: a 19 yr old , almost penniless. 4th October 2026, decades later: a life that has given India some of its most memorable words. This is the story of Javed Akhtar Some journeys begin with almost nothing. Except a dream. If he can do it so can you. Never give up," she added.For the unversed, Javed Akhtar and Shabana Azmi got married on 9 December 1984 and will be completing 42 years of marital bliss next month.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
